+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/arms-report.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.4 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
+#
+# report.sh --arms over a fixture results tree (the layout run-arms.sh
+# writes): the pre-registered verdicts, the bootstrap interval, refuted share,
+# missed labels, the refusal while STATUS.json is not complete and the
+# --partial header. Thresholds come from the real review-recall suite.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  REPORT="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/report.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ar.XXXXXX")"
+  R="$T/arms"; S="$R/review-recall"; B="$S/b1"
+  mkdir -p "$B"
+  jq -n '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", batch:"b1", dry_run:false, source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457",
+          model_id:"claude-fable-5-1", arms:["baseline","no_companion","no_karpathy","no_rule_files"], fixtures:["pr-01","pr-02","pr-03"], trials:3}' \
+    > "$B/MANIFEST.json"
+  status_file complete
+}
+
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+status_file() {  # status_file <state>
+  jq -n --arg s "$1" '{schema_version:1, suite:"review-recall", state:$s, batches:[{batch:"b1", state:$s}],
+                       source_commit:"864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457", model_id:"claude-fable-5-1"}' > "$S/STATUS.json"
+}
+
+# row <arm> <fixture> <trial> <recall> <missed-csv> [<cited> <refuted> <model> <source>]
+row() {
+  local arm="$1" fx="$2" t="$3" rc="$4" missed="$5" cited="${6:-4}" ref="${7:-1}"
+  local model="${8:-claude-fable-5-1}" src="${9:-864069f2f31c57dd00cd4e29e862d6c16d17c457}"
+  mkdir -p "$B/$arm"
+  jq -cn --arg arm "$arm" --arg fx "$fx" --argjson t "$t" --argjson rc "$rc" --arg missed "$missed" \
+    --argjson cited "$cited" --argjson ref "$ref" --arg model "$model" --arg src "$src" \
+    '{status:"completed", arm:$arm, fixture:$fx, task_id:("review-" + $fx), trial:$t, model_id:$model, source_commit:$src,
+      executor:{model_id:$model, usage:{input_tokens:100, cache_read_input_tokens:900, output_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}},
+      graders:[{name:"recall-vs-defects.sh", details:{recall:$rc, planted:3,
+        detected:[], missed:($missed | split(",") | map(select(length > 0))),
+        findings_cited:$cited, findings_refuted:$ref}}]}' >> "$B/$arm/results.jsonl"
+}
+
+full_arm() {  # full_arm <arm> <recall> [<missed>] [<refuted>]
+  local fx t
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row "$1" "$fx" "$t" "$2" "${3:-}" 4 "${4:-1}"; done; done
+}
+
+@test "AR-1 complete run: equal recall reads no recall loss, a large drop reads recall loss, the informational arm says so" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1
+  full_arm no_karpathy 0.3333 "L2,L3" 1
+  full_arm no_companion 1
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --date 2026-10-14
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*'
+  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
+  grep -E '^\| `no_companion` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q 'informational: yield only'
+  grep -E '^\| `baseline` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '(reference)'
+  # the interval of the drop and the missed labels are printed
+  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\[0.667, 0.667\]'
+  grep -q 'no_karpathy`: pr-01:L2 (3/3)' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -q '^# Control-arm report — 2026-10-14' "$T/r.md"
+  ! grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-2 a refuted-share rise beyond the threshold is a recall loss even with equal recall" {
+  full_arm baseline 1 "" 0
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1 "" 3
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*recall loss\*\*'
+  grep -q 'refuted share 0.750 > baseline 0.000' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-3 a missing trial or fixture is inconclusive; model or source skew is inconclusive" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_rule_files "$fx" "$t" 1 ""; done; done
+  row no_rule_files pr-03 1 1 ""
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_karpathy "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-opus-5-5; done; done
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do for t in 1 2 3; do row no_companion "$fx" "$t" 1 "" 4 1 claude-fable-5-1 ffd25258; done; done
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'coverage: pr-03 1/3' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -E '^\| `no_karpathy` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -q 'source skew' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-4 a rule violation within the baseline's own trial-to-trial spread names no change (inconclusive)" {
+  # baseline trial means 1.0, 0.6, 1.0 (spread 0.4); the arm sits 0.2 lower on every fixture
+  local fx
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row baseline "$fx" 1 1 ""; row baseline "$fx" 2 0.6 ""; row baseline "$fx" 3 1 ""; done
+  for fx in pr-01 pr-02 pr-03; do row no_rule_files "$fx" 1 0.8 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 2 0.4 ""; row no_rule_files "$fx" 3 0.8 ""; done
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'no change can be named' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-5 STATUS.json not complete: refused (exit 1); --partial writes, says so, and every verdict is inconclusive" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1
+  status_file running
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  grep -q "not 'complete'" <<<"$output"
+  [ ! -e "$T/r.md" ]
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md" --partial
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -q 'PARTIAL REPORT' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  ! grep -q '\*\*no recall loss\*\*' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-7 a safeguard-refusal fallback to another model is skew: the arm is inconclusive and the fallback is named" {
+  full_arm baseline 1
+  full_arm no_rule_files 1
+  # one no_rule_files trial moved to Opus on a refusal (models_used + refusal_fallbacks, as execute-agent records them)
+  jq -c 'if .trial == 1 and .fixture == "pr-01" then .executor.models_used = {"claude-fable-5-1": 10, "global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5": 90}
+         | .executor.refusal_fallbacks = [{"from":"claude-fable-5-1","to":"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5","category":"cyber"}] else . end' \
+    "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl" > "$B/x" && mv "$B/x" "$B/no_rule_files/results.jsonl"
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -E '^\| `no_rule_files` ' "$T/r.md" | grep -q '\*\*inconclusive\*\*'
+  grep -q 'model skew' "$T/r.md"
+  grep -q '1/9 trial(s) fell back to another model on a safeguard refusal' "$T/r.md"
+}
+
+@test "AR-6 the default output path is evals/results/arms-report-<date>.md under the results root's repo; bad args exit 2" {
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite nope --results-dir "$R"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --suite review-recall --results-dir "$T/missing" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+  run "$REPORT" --arms --date 14-10-2026 --results-dir "$R" --out "$T/r.md"
+  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/run-arms.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 Task 1.6 (FR-2, SDD D-2.3)
+#
+# run-arms.sh drives control arms over a frozen fixture batch against a
+# detached worktree pinned at --source-commit. The executor is the CLI stub
+# (no model call); the source repo is a throwaway repo (LOA_ARMS_SOURCE_REPO)
+# so no worktree is ever registered in the real repository; the results and
+# the worktree live under the test's temp dir.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  RA="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/run-arms.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ra.XXXXXX")"
+  SRC="$T/src"
+  mkdir -p "$SRC/.claude/loa" "$SRC/.claude/rules" "$SRC/.claude/skills/reviewing-code"
+  printf '%s\n' "# Loa" "" "## Karpathy Principles" "" "k" "" "## Other" > "$SRC/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  echo "# s" > "$SRC/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md"
+  echo "# i" > "$SRC/.claude/rules/skill-invariants.md"
+  printf '%s\n' "---" "name: reviewing-code" "---" "# Review" > "$SRC/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
+  printf '%s\n' "flatline_protocol:" "  code_review:" "    enabled: true" > "$SRC/.loa.config.yaml"
+  ( cd "$SRC" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -q -m src )
+  SHA="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  export LOA_ARMS_SOURCE_REPO="$SRC" LOA_ARMS_CACHE="$T/cache"
+  export EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub.sh"
+  # the stub writes a review that cites all three pr-01 defect anchors
+  export STUB_WRITE_1='review.md::# Review\nhead/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:210 and head/.claude/scripts/lib/invoke-diagnostics.sh:50 and head/.claude/scripts/workflow-state.sh:72 and head/.claude/scripts/workflow-state.sh:400\n'
+  RES="$T/results"
+  unset STUB_FAIL_COUNTER LOA_EVAL_ARM LOA_EVAL_ARM_TOGGLES
+}
+
+teardown() {
+  git -C "$SRC" worktree prune 2>/dev/null || true
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+@test "RA-1 --dry-run lists the interleaved plan and writes MANIFEST.json without a worktree or a CLI call" {

+    --source-commit "$SHA" --results-dir "$RES" --dry-run
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  grep -q 'planned trials: 8' <<<"$output"
+  # trial-major, then fixture, then arm: arms alternate on consecutive lines
+  [ "$(grep -E '^ +[0-9]+ ' <<<"$output" | awk '{print $2}' | head -4 | tr '\n' ,)" = "baseline,no_rule_files,baseline,no_rule_files," ]
+  [ "$(grep -E '^ +[0-9]+ ' <<<"$output" | awk '{print $3}' | head -4 | tr '\n' ,)" = "pr-01,pr-01,pr-02,pr-02," ]
+  M="$RES/review-recall/batch-pr-01-pr-02-n2/MANIFEST.json"
+  [ -f "$M" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.source_commit' "$M")" = "$SHA" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.model_id' "$M")" = "claude-fable-5-1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.dry_run' "$M")" = "true" ]

+  [ "$(jq -r '.corpus.sha256 | length' "$M")" = "64" ]
+  jq -e '.harness_commit and .executor.cli_version and .environment.os and .environment.yq' "$M" >/dev/null
+  [ ! -e "$T/cache/arms-src-${SHA:0:12}" ]
+  [ ! -e "$T/argv" ]

+  [ -z "$(git -C "$WT" status --porcelain)" ]
+  [ -f "$WT/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md" ]

+  # (exit 1, not 2: the gates run; pr-01 alone has no clean task for the false-positive gate)

+@test "RA-3 a transport failure is retried once; a second failure leaves the arm partial (exit 1, results kept)" {

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD §1.6, D-9.2)
+# The floor does not move: every floor_files entry of .claude/data/floor.yaml
+# and the fence-corpus rows named under floor_corpus are byte-identical to
+# origin/main; the register disables nothing, so the .claude/settings.json hook
+# registrations and the fence's pattern-id call-site list are identical too.
+# Skipped, with a message, when origin/main is not reachable (a shallow CI
+# checkout); the floor.yaml sha256 pin in guard-origins.bats still runs there.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
+  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+  if ! git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify -q 'origin/main^{commit}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    skip "origin/main is not reachable from this checkout (shallow clone?): the floor snapshot needs it — run 'git fetch origin main'"
+  fi
+  BASE="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse 'origin/main^{commit}')"
+}
+
+base_show() { git -C "$ROOT" show "$BASE:$1"; }
+
+@test "FS-1 every floor_files entry is byte-identical to origin/main" {
+  n=0
+  while IFS= read -r f; do
+    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
+    n=$((n + 1))
+    git -C "$ROOT" cat-file -e "$BASE:$f" || { echo "$f is not on origin/main" >&2; false; }
+    base_show "$f" | cmp -s - "$ROOT/$f" || { echo "floor file $f differs from origin/main" >&2; false; }
+  done < <(yq -r '.floor_files[]' "$FLOOR")
+  [ "$n" -ge 4 ]
+}
+
+@test "FS-2 the fence-corpus rows named in floor_corpus (FR-1.2b, FR-SZ*) are identical to origin/main" {
+  corpus="$(yq -r '.floor_corpus.file' "$FLOOR")"
+  rules="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.floor_corpus.rules' "$FLOOR")"
+  sel='def m($r): $r | any(.[]; . as $p | if ($p | endswith("*")) then ($in.rule // "" | startswith($p | rtrimstr("*"))) else ($in.rule // "") == $p end);
+       . as $in | select(m($rules))'
+  diff <(base_show "$corpus" | jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel") <(jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel" "$ROOT/$corpus")
+}
+
+@test "FS-3 the register disables nothing: settings.json hook registrations are identical to origin/main" {
+  diff <(base_show .claude/settings.json | jq -c '.hooks') <(jq -c '.hooks' "$ROOT/.claude/settings.json")
+}
+
+@test "FS-4 the fence's pattern-id call-site list (in order) is identical to origin/main" {
+  ids() { grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"'; }
+  diff <(base_show .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh | ids) <(ids < "$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh")
+}

+# =============================================================================

+# The origin map .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml covers every guard the
+# repository enumerates: every hook script registered in .claude/settings.json,
+# every fence pattern id in block-destructive-bash.sh, every validator rule
+# marker in validate-artifact.sh, the fixed gate list and the floor policies.
+# The enumeration here is independent of guard-yield.sh (its own jq/grep), so a
+# bug in the script cannot hide a gap. Fixture copies prove the failure modes.
+# =============================================================================
+
+# The sha256 of .claude/data/floor.yaml. An edit to the floor fails this suite
+# until the pin is updated deliberately, in the same change, with a reviewer:
+#   bash -c 'source .claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh; sha256_portable .claude/data/floor.yaml'
+FLOOR_SHA256="bd1f22dce9b6f18a0fda36d5a65dacd8103075c66c8c649b21de04fffcc92587"
+
+setup() {
+  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
+  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
+  MAP="$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml"
+  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+  SETTINGS="$ROOT/.claude/settings.json"
+  FENCE="$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+  VALIDATOR="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gorig.XXXXXX")"
+  # Fixture outputs never touch the tracked register or the live .run.
+  OUTARGS=(--out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run" --audit-log "$T/no-audit.jsonl")
+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+# ids of every registered hook script, derived independently of guard-yield.sh
+enumerated_hook_ids() {
+  jq -r '.hooks | to_entries[] | .value[] | .hooks[].command' "$SETTINGS" \
+    | grep -oE '\.claude/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.sh' | sed -e 's#^\.claude/##' \
+    | sed -e 's#^hooks/#hook:#' -e 's#^scripts/#hook:scripts/#' | sort -u
+}
+enumerated_fence_ids() {
+  grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$FENCE" | grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"' \
+    | sed -E 's/.*"([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)"$/fence:\1/' | sort -u
+}
+enumerated_validator_ids() {
+  grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*# @guard validator:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' "$VALIDATOR" | sed -E 's/.*validator:/validator:/' | sort -u
+}
+map_ids() { yq -r ".guards[] | select(.kind == \"$1\") | .id" "$MAP" | sort -u; }

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD §1.6, D-9.2)
+# The floor does not move: every floor_files entry of .claude/data/floor.yaml
+# and the fence-corpus rows named under floor_corpus are byte-identical to
+# origin/main; the register disables nothing, so the .claude/settings.json hook
+# registrations and the fence's pattern-id call-site list are identical too.
+# Skipped, with a message, when origin/main is not reachable (a shallow CI
+# checkout); the floor.yaml sha256 pin in guard-origins.bats still runs there.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
+  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+  if ! git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify -q 'origin/main^{commit}' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    skip "origin/main is not reachable from this checkout (shallow clone?): the floor snapshot needs it — run 'git fetch origin main'"
+  fi
+  BASE="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse 'origin/main^{commit}')"
+}
+
+base_show() { git -C "$ROOT" show "$BASE:$1"; }
+
+@test "FS-1 every floor_files entry is byte-identical to origin/main" {
+  n=0
+  while IFS= read -r f; do
+    [ -n "$f" ] || continue
+    n=$((n + 1))
+    git -C "$ROOT" cat-file -e "$BASE:$f" || { echo "$f is not on origin/main" >&2; false; }
+    base_show "$f" | cmp -s - "$ROOT/$f" || { echo "floor file $f differs from origin/main" >&2; false; }
+  done < <(yq -r '.floor_files[]' "$FLOOR")
+  [ "$n" -ge 4 ]
+}

+@test "FS-2 the fence-corpus rows named in floor_corpus (FR-1.2b, FR-SZ*) are identical to origin/main" {
+  corpus="$(yq -r '.floor_corpus.file' "$FLOOR")"
+  rules="$(yq -o=json -I0 '.floor_corpus.rules' "$FLOOR")"
+  sel='def m($r): $r | any(.[]; . as $p | if ($p | endswith("*")) then ($in.rule // "" | startswith($p | rtrimstr("*"))) else ($in.rule // "") == $p end);
+       . as $in | select(m($rules))'
+  diff <(base_show "$corpus" | jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel") <(jq -c --argjson rules "$rules" "$sel" "$ROOT/$corpus")
+}
+
+@test "FS-3 the register disables nothing: settings.json hook registrations are identical to origin/main" {
+  diff <(base_show .claude/settings.json | jq -c '.hooks') <(jq -c '.hooks' "$ROOT/.claude/settings.json")

+@test "FS-4 the fence's pattern-id call-site list (in order) is identical to origin/main" {

+#!/usr/bin/env bats

+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/guard-origins.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 AC-1.1, SDD D-1.6)
+# The origin map .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml covers every guard the
+# repository enumerates: every hook script registered in .claude/settings.json,
+# every fence pattern id in block-destructive-bash.sh, every validator rule
+# marker in validate-artifact.sh, the fixed gate list and the floor policies.
+# The enumeration here is independent of guard-yield.sh (its own jq/grep), so a
+# bug in the script cannot hide a gap. Fixture copies prove the failure modes.
+# =============================================================================
+
+# The sha256 of .claude/data/floor.yaml. An edit to the floor fails this suite
+# until the pin is updated deliberately, in the same change, with a reviewer:
+#   bash -c 'source .claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh; sha256_portable .claude/data/floor.yaml'
+FLOOR_SHA256="bd1f22dce9b6f18a0fda36d5a65dacd8103075c66c8c649b21de04fffcc92587"
+
+setup() {
+  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
+  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
+  MAP="$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml"
+  FLOOR="$ROOT/.claude/data/floor.yaml"
+  SETTINGS="$ROOT/.claude/settings.json"
+  FENCE="$ROOT/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
+  VALIDATOR="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gorig.XXXXXX")"
+  # Fixture outputs never touch the tracked register or the live .run.
+  OUTARGS=(--out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run" --audit-log "$T/no-audit.jsonl")
+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+# ids of every registered hook script, derived independently of guard-yield.sh
+enumerated_hook_ids() {
+  jq -r '.hooks | to_entries[] | .value[] | .hooks[].command' "$SETTINGS" \
+    | grep -oE '\.claude/[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+\.sh' | sed -e 's#^\.claude/##' \
+    | sed -e 's#^hooks/#hook:#' -e 's#^scripts/#hook:scripts/#' | sort -u
+}
+enumerated_fence_ids() {
+  grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#' "$FENCE" | grep -oE 'emit_block "[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"|pattern_id(: |=)"[A-Za-z0-9._-]+"' \
+    | sed -E 's/.*"([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)"$/fence:\1/' | sort -u
+}
+enumerated_validator_ids() {
+  grep -oE '^[[:space:]]*# @guard validator:[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' "$VALIDATOR" | sed -E 's/.*validator:/validator:/' | sort -u
+}
+map_ids() { yq -r ".guards[] | select(.kind == \"$1\") | .id" "$MAP" | sort -u; }

+# One sprint block; $1 = the Technical Tasks lines (printf-ready, one per line).

+    printf '### Sprint Goal\ng\n\n### Deliverables\n- [ ] d\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n- [ ] c\n\n'
+    printf '### Technical Tasks\n%s\n\n' "$1"

+    printf '### Success Metrics\n- m\n\n'

+# $1 = header date (may be empty); $2 = sprint 1 task lines; $3 = the E2E task line.

+- [x] Task 1.2: done already · kind:mechanical
+```
+- [ ] not a task
+```' "$E2E" > "$T/sprint.md"
+    run "$SCRIPT" --type sprint --file "$T/sprint.md"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
+# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
+#
+#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
+#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>

+#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
+#
+# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
+#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
+#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
+#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
+#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
+#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
+#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
+#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
+#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
+#                  binary files skipped)
+#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
+#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
+#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
+#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
+#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
+#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
+#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
+#
+# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
+# default to paths under its top level.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
+#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
+#
+#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
+#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
+#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
+#
+# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
+# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
+# =============================================================================
+set -euo pipefail
+export LC_ALL=C
+
+usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
+die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
+
+SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
+
+FROM=""
+TO=""
+PLAN=""
+MODELINV=""
+JSON=0
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
+      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
+      case "$1" in
+        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
+        --to) TO="$2" ;;
+        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
+        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
+      esac
+      shift 2 ;;
+    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
+    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+done
+
+[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
+command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
+TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
+[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
+[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
+[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
+[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
+
+# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
+case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
+case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
+FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
+TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
+
+# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
+kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
+  md_fence($0) { next }
+  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
+  !insp { next }
+  /^### / {
+    sec = 0
+    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
+    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
+    next
+  }
+  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
+  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
+  {
+    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
+      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
+      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
+      n[v]++
+    } else n["untagged"]++
+  }
+  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
+' "$PLAN")"
+read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
+[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
+
+# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
+GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
+SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
+  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
+PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
+  | awk '
+      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
+      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
+      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
+      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
+      END { printf "%d\n", s }
+    ')"
+
+# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
+FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
+TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
+MODEL_CALLS=""
+if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
+  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
+      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
+      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
+      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
+      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
+    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+else
+  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
+fi
+
+iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -n \
+    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
+    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
+    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
+    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
+    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
+    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
+    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
+      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
+      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
+               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
+               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
+else
+  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
+  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
+    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
+fi

+FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
+TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
+MODEL_CALLS=""
+if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
+  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
+      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
+      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
+      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
+      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
+    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+else
+  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
+fi
+
+iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
+
+if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
+  jq -n \
+    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
+    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
+    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
+    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
+    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
+    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
+    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
+      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
+      volume: {script_lines_changed: $script_lines, prose_bytes_changed: $prose_bytes,
+               model_calls: (if $calls == "" then null else ($calls | tonumber) end),
+               scope: "host", modelinv: $modelinv}}'
+else
+  printf 'kinds: mechanical %s · judgment %s · operator %s\n' "$K_MECH" "$K_JUDG" "$K_OPER"
+  printf "volume: script lines changed %s (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed %s (*.md) · model calls %s (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: %s\n" \
+    "$SCRIPT_LINES" "$PROSE_BYTES" "${MODEL_CALLS:-n/a}" "$MODELINV"
+fi

# Reviewer concerns — sprint-1 (PR: sprint-255, cycle-129)

Scope: `pr/head.diff`, 81 files. The fixture excludes `grimoires/`, so the generated register
`grimoires/loa/guards.md` and the record corpus under `evals/fixtures/review-prs/` could not be
inspected; findings below are about the files present.

## Concerns to probe

1. `evals/harness/run-arms.sh` — re-running the same deterministic default batch name after a
   partial run appends duplicate trial rows to `<arm>/results.jsonl` and resets the per-arm
   STATUS counters (DONE/FAILED start at 0; MANIFEST.json is rewritten). `arms-report.py`
   counts every row per fixture, so coverage can be satisfied by duplicates.
2. `evals/harness/run-arms.sh` — `date +%s%N | cut -c1-13` is GNU-only; the script claims bash 3.2
   (macOS) compatibility. On BSD date the arithmetic `$(( end_ms - start_ms ))` is a syntax
   error inside the background job → no row → trial FAILED.
3. `evals/harness/run-arms.sh` — `is_transport_failure` greps `agent-output.json` for
   `network`, `5[0-9][0-9] `: model prose in the result text can classify a genuine agent
   error as transport and trigger a retry.
4. `evals/harness/run-arms.sh` — `aggregate_status` passes `$(find …)` unquoted to jq; a
   results dir with spaces breaks it; `--results-dir` is not validated.
5. `evals/harness/execute-agent.sh` — arm mode copies the prompt tree's `.loa.config.yaml` over
   any config the fixture itself carried; `karpathy_block` toggle rewrites `constraints.json`
   with `(.constraints // []) |=` creating the key when absent.
6. `evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh` — `REDACTED` counter is incremented for the diff
   text and again for each base/head file (`redact(b)` with count=True), so the dropped.txt
   note over-reports; binary rename detection `p.split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")` mishandles
   `dir/{old => new}/file`.
7. `evals/harness/arms-report.py` — `sorted({m.get('source_commit') …})` raises TypeError when
   a manifest lacks the key (None vs str).
8. `.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh` — the replay heuristic's `$tmp` prefix is the generator's
   own TMPDIR; `TMPDIR=/` would classify every row as replay. `"$AUDIT_LOG".*` glob also reads
   `.lock`/`.bak` siblings as segments.
9. `.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md` — `app.permission` changed read → read-write; not
   named in the PR title; check whether it is intended (SURGICAL).
10. `.github/workflows/check-prompt-budget.yml` + `tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats` PB-10 — the
    header comment now states 160,000 / 114,688; `tools/check-prompt-budget.sh` is not in the
    change, so the pin depends on constants outside the diff.
11. `.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh validate_sprint_kinds` — the J heuristic and the
    `T`/`U` classification; `[[ "$plan_date" < … ]]` string compare.
12. `evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh` — refuted-share regions and ±3 widening consistent with
    the detection rule?

input.content:
# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md
**Change under review:** `pr/head.diff` — feat(cycle-129): sprint-255 — guard register with origin and yield, pre-registered control arms on a record corpus, task kinds, path-scoped rule files (81 files)

---

## Overall Assessment

This is a large, well-tested change. The guard register (`guard-yield.sh`, `guard-origins.yaml`, `floor.yaml`) is internally consistent: regenerating the register from the PR's origin map, the PR's fence and validator markers and the live hook settings reproduces the PR's `hooks-reference.md` table byte for byte, `--check` reports in sync (95 guards), and every bats suite I could run against the head files passes (guard-origins 15/15, guard-yield 11/11, validate-artifact sprint-kinds 11/11, cycle-ratio 6/6, loa-status-guards 3/3, arms-report 7/7, arm-toggles 11/11, recall grader RG-28, compare BF-10..13, execute-agent EA-11/12). The task-kind validator, the kind-count tool and the control-arm toggles do what their tests say.

One defect blocks: `run-arms.sh` is not idempotent on its own deterministic batch name. The script explicitly admits a second run into a batch that already holds results for the same source and model, then re-plans every trial from scratch, appends duplicate rows to `results.jsonl`, overwrites the per-trial artifacts and resets the STATUS counters. `arms-report.py` counts every row, so the pre-registered verdict that licenses deleting a control can be computed over duplicated trials while STATUS.json reads `complete`. Several medium observations follow, three of them raised by the cross-model dissent (two voices, no rejected payloads).

Scope note: the fixture excludes `grimoires/` and the record corpus under `evals/fixtures/review-prs/`, so the tracked register `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, the eight record fixtures, their hidden labels and `SHA256SUMS` could not be inspected; nothing below claims a defect in them. The implementation report (`reviewer.md`) is the PR description and carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; the verdict below rests on the code finding, not on that omission.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Control-arm driver: re-running a batch duplicates trials and corrupts the verdict inputs

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:255-257` — a second `run-arms.sh` invocation on an existing batch with the same source commit and model is admitted, re-plans every trial, appends duplicate rows and resets the counters, so the control-arm report and STATUS.json no longer describe one experiment.
**File:** `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:255-257` (admission), `:126` (deterministic default batch name), `:264` (counters restart at 0), `:408` (rows appended with `>>`), `:409-420` (artifacts copied over the previous trial's), `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:135` and `:239` (every row is a cell; coverage counts duplicates)
**Issue:** The default `--batch` is a pure function of the fixture list (`batch-pr-01-pr-08-n8`). The pre-flight at lines 251-256 refuses a batch only when the recorded source or model differs; with the same pair it falls through to `write_manifest` (overwriting MANIFEST.json), rebuilds `PLAN` from scratch, starts `DONE`/`FAILED` at zero and appends each new row to `<arm>/results.jsonl` without reading what is already there. There is no resume, skip or de-duplication path. The script's own exit contract ("1 partial (some trial failed twice; results kept)") invites exactly this re-run to fill the gaps.
**Why This Matters:** `arms-report.py` is the pre-registered gate that may license removing a guard. After a re-run it sees two (or more) rows per (fixture, trial) cell: `fixture_means` and `trial_means` are biased toward whichever run was duplicated, `coverage_gaps` is satisfied by duplicates, `trials done` exceeds `trials_planned`, and STATUS.json still says `complete` with `trials_done` counting only the last run. The artifacts under `trial-N/` are overwritten while both rows survive, so the row/artifact pairing is broken. `run-arms.bats` RA-3 re-runs only with fresh `--batch` names, so the suite never exercises this path.
**Required Fix:** Either refuse a batch whose `<arm>/results.jsonl` already exists ("use another --batch", the same shape as line 255), or implement a real resume: read existing rows, skip (arm, fixture, trial) cells that already have a `completed` row, seed `DONE`/`FAILED` from them and keep MANIFEST.json. Add an RA test that re-runs the same batch and asserts one row per cell.
**Reference:** SDD D-2.3 (pre-registered verdict rule; the report must be computed over the planned cells exactly once).

---

## Observations

### 1. Guard register and floor

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:470` — the heredoc classifier is sourced into the generator's own process; a lib whose sourced fence does not honour library mode runs the fence as a hook and ends `guard-yield.sh` with exit 0 and nothing written.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:470`
**Suggestion:** Observed directly: with a `heredoc-classifier.sh` that sources the fence (`BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source …`) and a fence without that mode, the trace stops at `source` and the script exits 0 before `install_file`; `--check` cannot catch it because it exits before the yield section. Call `heredoc_nonexec` through a subshell (`( source …; heredoc_nonexec "$cmd" )`) or verify the lib with `bash -n`/a probe in a subshell before sourcing, and treat a missing summary line as failure.
**Benefit:** The yield generation cannot silently produce no files while reporting success.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:42-50` — the floor advertises protections it does not pin: `implement_gate.*` is a floor key while `gate:implement-gate` and `hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh` are `floor: false` (`head/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml:810`); `policy:permission-deny-list` is enforced by `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.json`, which `floor_files` does not pin (FS-3 pins only `.hooks`); `policy:operator-only-commands` is enforced by each command's `disable-model-invocation` frontmatter, not by `user-invoked-commands.txt` alone. Raised by the companion dissent (DISS-C-003).
**Suggestion:** Pin `.claude/settings.json` (or diff its `permissions.deny` against `settings.deny.json` in floor-snapshot.bats), cross-check `user-invoked-commands.txt` against the command files' frontmatter, and make `floor_keys` and the `floor:` rows agree on implement-gate.
**Benefit:** A cycle task cannot loosen a floor artefact while both floor suites stay green.

### 2. Rule files and skill frontmatter

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2-6` — path-scoping the stash rule to `*.sh`, `*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**` makes the prose guard conditional on which files are edited, but `git stash push/pop … | tail -1` is typed into Bash regardless of the files in play; in an app-code session only the harness regex (FR-1.2b) remains. Raised by the companion dissent (DISS-C-001); rule-paths.bats attributes the globs to SDD D-3.1 / DEC-0129, so this is a recorded decision, flagged here as a residual risk.
**Suggestion:** Record in the DEC row that the fence, not the prose, is the only stash guard in non-shell sessions, or widen the globs.
**Benefit:** The decision's cost is explicit where the floor is reasoned about.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:28` — `zones.app.permission` changes from `read` to `read-write`. SURGICAL: the PR title names the guard register, control arms, task kinds and path-scoped rule files; this hunk is none of them and is not explained in the diff. Also raised by the companion dissent (DISS-C-002).
**Suggestion:** The value is probably right (`/implement` is the skill that writes app code and `reviewing-code/SKILL.md` now points at the frontmatter as the zone source), but a security-relevant declaration should move with a one-line rationale or a DEC row.
**Benefit:** Anything that later consumes `zones:` (validate-skill-capabilities.sh, implement-gate) inherits an audited change, not drift.

### 3. Control-arm harness

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:326` — `date +%s%N | cut -c1-13` is GNU-only; on BSD/macOS `date` prints a literal `N`, so `$(( end_ms - start_ms ))` is an arithmetic error inside the background job under `set -e`, no row is written and every trial is `FAILED (no row written)`. The script states bash 3.2 compatibility (line 263) and the default model id was probed on a local CLI.
**Suggestion:** Use `python3 -c 'import time;print(int(time.time()*1000))'` (python3 is already a required tool) or seconds via `date +%s`.
**Benefit:** The driver runs where its author's own comments say it should.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314` — `is_transport_failure` greps `agent-output.json` for `network` and `5[0-9][0-9] `; the executor's result text (a review that mentions a network call or a line number followed by a space) can classify a genuine agent error as transport and spend the one retry.

Review of sprint-1 (task review-r19) is complete. The feedback file is written and its trailer self-checks as consistent.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.** Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md`, with the brief's one-line-per-finding shape mirrored in `review.md` at the repository root.

**What blocks the merge.** The control-arm driver `run-arms.sh` is not idempotent. A second run on the same batch with the same source commit and model is admitted on purpose, but it then re-plans every trial, appends duplicate rows to each arm's results file, overwrites the per-trial artifacts and restarts the STATUS counters at zero. The default batch name is deterministic and the script's own exit contract invites a re-run after a partial result, so this is the normal path, not an edge case. The arms report counts every row, so the pre-registered verdict that can license deleting a guard would be computed over duplicated trials while STATUS reads complete. The test suite only re-runs with fresh batch names, so it never sees this.

**What I verified rather than read.** Regenerating the guard register from the PR's origin map, fence and validator markers plus the live hook settings reproduced the PR's hooks table byte for byte, and the drift gate reported in sync. I ran twelve of the PR's bats suites against the head code on a scratch root and all passed, apart from two cases bound to files the fixture does not carry. The cross-model dissent ran with two voices, returned three advisory findings and rejected no payloads. Those three are triaged as medium observations: the floor pins indirect artefacts and disagrees with itself on implement-gate, the stash-safety rule is now path-scoped although stash commands happen in every session, and the implement skill's app-zone permission widened to read-write with no rationale in the diff.

**Other observations** cover a GNU-only `date` call that breaks the driver on macOS despite its bash 3.2 claim, a sourced heredoc library that can end `guard-yield.sh` with exit 0 and no output, and several low items in the seed script, the arms report and the transport-retry heuristic.

**Out of scope.** The fixture excludes `grimoires/` and the record corpus, so the tracked register and the eight record fixtures could not be inspected. The implementation report is the bare PR description with no AC walkthrough; I noted it but did not count it as a code finding.

**Next.** The engineer should refuse or resume a batch that already holds results, add a same-batch re-run test, decide the three declaration observations with a DEC row each, and request another review.
